One Oct-9 Reuters/Star piece citing 9to5Mac said Nov 6; every other source, including the earnings-watcher options page as of 2026-11-02, says Nov 2 amc.
conviction_note: Sept-quarter print likely at the top of Apple's own guide (consensus already sits there), so the reaction turns on the December-quarter guide and gross margin; the stock goes in at a record ($348.91 on 10-29, +14% since the last print, 38x forward, mean PT $328 below spot) after selling a beat -7.4% on guide and memory costs in July, while the December evidence is split (Duo sold out to January vs Pro order cuts, Loop 79M vs 85M units, memory costs); hence a mild down lean, p_up 44 on abs 4.5 against an implied 4.0. The findings sum (-1.8) is larger than the scaled number (-0.54) because the scaled number carries the sign uncertainty in p_up; they agree in sign.

findings.finding: Supply-chain and analyst evidence that December-quarter iPhone 18 Pro volumes are being cut: Nikkei Asia (2026-10-09) reported October component orders for 18 Pro/Pro Max cut at least 15-20% from Apple's original request; Loop Capital (2026-10-20, downgrade to Hold, PT $330) models 79M December-quarter iPhones vs ~85M Street and ASP $1,123 vs $1,239, citing a 13M-unit second-half cut it no longer expects recovered; Jefferies (2026-10-19) says China Pro lead times have fallen to zero with 10-15% component cuts. Against a Street iPhone bar of ~$93B for the December quarter (+9% on $85.3B a year ago) with no base iPhone 18 until spring 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 30 2026: record quarter and EPS beat ($2.02 vs $1.89), but September guide of +9-11% vs ~12% Street with supply constraints sent the stock -7.4% close to close (earnings-watcher; trendingtopics). The guide is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: All three are public and the stock has since made a record close (348.91 on 10-29), so the market has looked through them; if it believed 79M units the stock would not sit 6% above the mean PT of $328 at 38x forward. It is unpriced only to the extent Apple's guide confirms the unit cut. Apple does not guide units, so the test is the total revenue range against ~$153.4B.
findings.independence: Nikkei via The Star https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/10/09/apple-cuts-iphone-18-pro-orders-due-to-soft-demand-nikkei-asia-reports- (2026-10-09, Apple unconfirmed); Jefferies via https://www.roic.ai/news/apples-iphone-18-pro-demand-weakens-jefferies-warns-but-foldable-duo-sees-strong-backlog-10-19-2026. Counter: JPMorgan 2026-10-12 says Pro demand marginally stronger than 17 Pro at the same stage and raised PT to $360 (https://macdailynews.com/2026/09/28/iphone-18-pro-demand-looks-healthy-as-lead-times-barely-ease-jpmorgan/); Macworld argues the cuts free components for the Duo (https://macworld.com/article/3257381/those-iphone-18-pro-production-cuts-are-actually-a-really-good-sign.html). Three sources, one thesis: filed once.

findings.finding: iPhone Duo (foldable, from $1,999, on sale 2026-10-23) pre-orders sold out within hours on 2026-10-16 with US shipping dates slipping to late January 2027; Apple told the FT demand is 'nothing short of extraordinary'; supply for the rest of 2026 reportedly capped near 10M units (Securities Times via iDevice), Counterpoint expects ~6M shipped by year end. At ~$2,000+ ASP, 6-10M units is roughly $12-20B of December-quarter revenue that did not exist last year, against a December revenue bar of ~$153.4B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior new-category launch inside this reaction window; April 30 2026 (+3.2%) was the last print where the guide (+13-16% revenue growth for the March quarter) beat expectations.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell-out is public and part of why the stock made a record; what is not priced is how many units Apple can actually build, which only the December revenue guide reveals. If the market had priced a 10M-unit quarter, Street December revenue would sit well above +6.7% y/y; at $153.4B it looks like ~6M units at most, net of the Pro cuts.
findings.independence: Supply cap ~10M: https://idevice.com/iphone-duo-orders-placed-now-ship-in-late-november.md ; Counterpoint 6M: https://idevice.com/counterpoint-expects-6-million-iphone-duos-shipped-by-year-end ; Jefferies notes Duo 90+ day waits in China (roic.ai link above). Note the Duo may be absorbing components cut from the Pro, so this and the order-cut finding partly offset by construction; both kept, opposite signs, net about zero.

findings.finding: December-quarter gross margin risk from memory: Apple said in July the memory cost increase exceeded the whole sequential GM decline into the September guide (47-48% incl ~1pt tariff refunds, ~46.5% underlying) and that the carry-in inventory benefit declines beyond September; SK hynix (2026-10-28) posted record Q3 profit and says DRAM shortage runs through 2030; Bernstein (2026-09-25) models December GM 46.2% vs ~46.7% consensus and iPhone GM 40.4%, 390bp below consensus, EPS $2.87 vs $2.92. TrendForce's 3Q26 mobile DRAM report expects contract prices to enter 'high-level consolidation' in 4Q26, a partial offset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 30 2026: GM guide cut to 47-48% on memory costs ('we expect to pay even higher memory costs going forward') was half of the -7.4% reaction (itiger https://www.itiger.com/news/1175106371).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock rose after Bernstein's note and sits at a record; consensus GM of ~46.7% for December is above Bernstein and above the September underlying 46.5%, i.e. the Street assumes holiday mix and Duo offset memory. If the market priced Bernstein, consensus FY27 GM (47.4%, TIKR) would already be lower.
findings.independence: SK hynix 3Q26 release https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/sk-hynix-announces-3q26-financial-results-20261028 (shortage through 2030: https://iphonewired.com/industry/1200227/); Apple 10-Q for the June quarter says supply constraints and component cost increases are expected 'to intensify' and gross margins face 'downward pressure' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019326000020/aapl-20260627.htm). Counter: TrendForce 4Q26 consolidation https://www.trendforce.com/research/download/RP260909CK.

findings.finding: UBS, citing Sensor Tower, puts September-quarter App Store revenue growth at about +2% y/y (September +5%), low single digits for a second quarter; US commission revenue reportedly down 18% since the start of 2026; Services missed Visible Alpha consensus by 2.1% in the June quarter at +12%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June quarter Services miss (+12%, 2.1% below consensus) was noted but the guide drove the -7.4% (S&P Global post-Q3 note, https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/08/apple-postq-iphone-strength-drives-beat-supply-and-memory-costs-cloud-outlook).
findings.why_not_priced: App Store is part of Services (~27% of revenue, a larger share of gross profit); previews still frame Services as 'growth could slip below 10%' rather than as a miss. Net of the rest: hardware (iPhone at the mid-teens guide) is ~73% of revenue, so a 1-2 point Services shortfall costs about 0.3-0.5% of total revenue, inside the guided range.
findings.independence: US commission -18%: https://www.mactech.com/2026/08/18/apples-u-s-commission-revenue-has-fallen-18-since-the-start-of-2026/ (a different series, also Sensor Tower-based).

findings.finding: Setup: the stock enters the print at a record ($348.91 close on 2026-10-29, $344.63 on 10-30), +14.1% since the July report against +2.1% for the S&P 500, ~38x forward P/E at the top of its five-year range, mean analyst PT $328 (~6% below spot); in July a record beat with a below-Street guide was sold -7.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last six prints close-to-close: -7.4, +3.2, +0.5, -0.4, -2.5, -3.7: four of six down, and the two strong beats (July 2026, May 2025) both fell on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: This is what is priced, not what is missed: the finding is that the bar for the December guide is high. If the market had priced the downside, the stock would not be 18% above its 200-day average into a print with these December unit cuts in the public record.
findings.independence: finviz/StockStory 2026-10-26 (+14.1% since last report, 18% above 200dma, 'little room for an in-line quarter'): https://finviz.com/news/407895/apple-heads-into-ternus-era-with-memory-costs-and-supply-limits-testing-a-rally ; prices from statmuse. Short interest ~1% of float, so no squeeze offset.

findings.finding: IDC's preliminary CQ3 2026 tracker (2026-10-15) has Apple shipping 57.3M iPhones, -4.0% y/y, at a record 22.4% share in a market down 22.0% on memory costs; Counterpoint attributes the decline to the missing base iPhone 18. Apple's guide of mid-teens iPhone revenue growth therefore requires ASP up ~20% from a Pro-only launch plus the $100 price rise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Apple guided iPhone mid-teens knowing the launch mix; the line was met in July (iPhone +22% vs guide). No case in the history of IDC units moving the print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: lands inside what Apple guided (the base-model shift was planned). What would be visible if it were a miss: S&P's $56.4B iPhone estimate (+15%) would have come down after 10-15; it was not reported as cut.
findings.independence: Counterpoint/Omdia ~20% market decline, Apple down: https://androidheadlines.com/2026/10/global-smartphone-market-shrank-20-in-q3-2026-samsung-apple-dominate.html. One IDC document; the 22% market figure is merged here.

findings.finding: Counterpoint: iPhone 18 Pro series sales in the first three weeks were +3.1% y/y globally vs the iPhone 17 Pro series, +29% in China, -4% in the US and -27% in Japan; Apple took 33% of China week-38 sales while the China market was -17%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Greater China +22% in the June quarter and +38% in December 2025; China strength accompanied the +0.5% (Jan 2026) and -7.4% (July 2026) reactions, so it has not driven the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month; partly priced. Only ~9 days of Pro sell-through fall in the September quarter, so it informs Greater China in the print and the December guide; Counterpoint itself flags possible front-loading.
findings.independence: Three-week global/China split: https://www.gadgetreview.com/?p=424070 ; SCMP https://scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3369323/apple-leads-china-smartphone-sales-after-launch-iphone-18-pro-can-momentum-last . All Counterpoint; one data source.

findings.finding: Apple's June-quarter 10-Q shows manufacturing purchase obligations of $57.0B ($56.2B within 12 months), up from $44.6B in the March-quarter 10-Q, a $12.4B (+28%) build in one quarter, beside 10-Q language that supply constraints and component cost increases are expected to intensify.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a line the stock has traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Not in previews or the wire. Financing-style question: what does it buy? Read as securing components for the 18 Pro and Duo ramp (corroborated by the Duo sell-out and Apple's 'supply constraints' framing), it supports December supply; read as locking memory at peak prices it is a margin headwind. The two cancel, so sized small positive on the supply reading.
findings.independence: Prior-quarter figure: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019326000013/aapl-20260328.htm . Same filer, two documents.

findings.finding: TSMC's 3Q26 results (2026-10-15/16): smartphone revenue +~10% q/q (21% of revenue), while C.C. Wei said consumer and price-sensitive markets face headwinds from rising component prices; analysts attributed part of the strength to inventory builds ahead of launches.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No case in the history of TSMC's smartphone line moving Apple's print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy for A20 wafer sell-in, public two weeks; consistent with the iPhone guide being met and says little about the December guide.

findings.finding: Foxconn (Apple's main iPhone assembler) reported Q3 revenue +47% y/y on AI servers, but monthly reporting said September smart consumer electronics revenue was flat as higher retail pricing curtailed unit shipments, while the company called the quarter's segment growth 'significant'.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy, public for four weeks; flat September consumer electronics during the Pro launch month fits fewer units at higher ASP, which is what Apple guided.
findings.independence: Proxy; Reuters via The Star https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/10/05/foxconn-third-quarter-revenue-jumps-47-yy-beats-market-forecast ; agrees with IDC units -4%.

findings.finding: This is John Ternus's first earnings call as CEO (took over 2026-09-01, Cook executive chair; 8-K/A item 5.02 filed 2026-09-01), with CFO Kevan Parekh; any change in how Apple frames the guide (e.g. more or less on supply, memory or units) lands in this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO-transition call in the window; Ternus appeared on the April 2026 call (+3.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: No signed information; raises the dispersion rather than the mean, and is reflected in abs_move_pct, not in the sign.

outside_window.finding: Foxconn's full Q3 earnings (Nov 12 or 14) and October monthly revenue (~Nov 5) will give the first read on Duo/Pro assembly volumes in the December quarter.

baseline_tension: The baseline is empty; against the sourced substitutes, the down lean agrees with the run-up to a record (a high bar for the guide) and with the name's habit of selling beats on the guide, and there is no skew number to check it against; the evidence on the December guide itself is split, which is why p_up sits at 44 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the December revenue bar ($153.4B) has one source, so the two December unit findings were capped smaller: Pro order cuts -1.0 to -0.8, Duo +1.0 to +0.8; the GM finding keeps -1.0 because its bar has two roughly agreeing sources (Bernstein 46.7% consensus, TIKR 46.5% threshold).
Rule 6 (inside the guide) and rule 5 (proxy): IDC units -4% lands inside what Apple guided (mid-teens iPhone revenue on a planned Pro-only launch), -0.3 to -0.1.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Services/App Store -0.5 to -0.4, net of hardware being ~73% of revenue.
Rule 7: short interest looked up (~1% of float), not crowded, no shrink for squeeze; skew not found, recorded.
Last section (history rebuilt from confirmed releases): earnings-watcher reaction dates checked against the 8-K item 2.02 dates on EDGAR; they match.
